parts.label: a
parts.technique: Binomial expansion of (1+ax)^n for rational n
parts.reason: P4.1 covers binomial expansion for rational n including approximation; finding a from matching coefficient is standard application.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Binomial expansion coefficient
parts.reason: Same as (a), continuation of binomial expansion of (1+ax)^n, P4.1 covers this.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Product of binomial expansion with linear factor
parts.reason: Uses binomial expansion result from (b); P4.1 explicitly notes expansion 'may be used with expansion of rational functions by decomposition into partial fractions' and general algebraic manipulation of series, in spec.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Trapezium rule
parts.reason: P9.4 explicitly covers numerical integration using trapezium rule.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Integration using trig identities/double angle to find exact area
parts.reason: P8.3 covers area under curve via definite integral; integration of sin2x sinx uses double angle/product-to-sum identities covered by P5.6/P8.2 (trig identities integration).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Implicit differentiation
parts.reason: P7.5 explicitly covers differentiating functions defined implicitly, including finding tangents/normals to implicit curves.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Equation of tangent line using implicit derivative
parts.reason: P7.5 guidance explicitly states finding equations of tangents and normals to curves given implicitly is required.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Volume of revolution about x-axis
parts.reason: Volume of revolution is explicitly listed among concepts no 9MA0 statement covers, so this is out regardless of the integration technique used.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Finding constant in differential equation given rate of change
parts.reason: P7.6 covers constructing/using differential equations, substituting given rate to find constant - basic application.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Separation of variables, definite integral to find time
parts.reason: P8.7 covers analytical solution of first order separable differential equations including finding particular solutions/definite time values.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Connected rates of change to find volume
parts.reason: Uses dV/dt = dV/dh · dh/dt style connected rates of change and integration, covered by P7.4 guidance and P8.1/8.2 integration.

parts.label: i
parts.technique: Integration of e^{kx} type function
parts.reason: P8.2 covers integrating e^{kx} and related constant multiples.

parts.label: ii(a)
parts.technique: Partial fractions decomposition
parts.reason: P2.10 covers decomposing rational functions into partial fractions with denominators as products of linear terms, matches this case.

parts.label: ii(b)
parts.technique: Integration using partial fractions
parts.reason: P8.6 explicitly covers integrating using partial fractions that are linear in the denominator.

parts.label: iii
parts.technique: Integration by parts including ln x integral
parts.reason: P8.5 explicitly covers integration by parts and states the integral of ln x is required; this problem uses integration by parts with ln(2x).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Parametric differentiation dy/dx
parts.reason: P3.3 covers parametric equations of curves and P7.5 covers differentiating parametrically defined relations for first derivative; standard combination.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Finding normal to parametric curve using trig identities
parts.reason: Uses parametric differentiation (P7.5), exact trig values (P5.3) and equation of a straight line (P3.1); all covered.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Solving simultaneous equations (parametric curve and line) using trig identities/quadratic
parts.reason: Requires substituting parametric equations into line equation and solving quadratic in sin θ using double angle identity (P5.6) and quadratic solving (P2.3); this is curve/line intersection in Cartesian-parametric context, not a vector-line intersection, so it's in spec.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Distance between two points using position vectors
parts.reason: P10.4 covers position vectors and distance between two points represented by position vectors; finding P's coordinates uses substitution into a vector line but the required technique (distance calculation) itself is in spec.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Vector equation of a line through a point parallel to another line
parts.reason: Vector equation of a line (r = a + λb) is explicitly listed among concepts no 9MA0 statement covers, so writing down such an equation is out of spec.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Angle between two vectors using scalar (dot) product
parts.reason: Scalar (dot) product including angle between vectors/lines is explicitly listed among concepts no 9MA0 statement covers; excluded.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Finding point on a line using vector methods (dot product/distance equality)
parts.reason: Depends on line l2 (out of spec, part b) and uses dot product/vector line algebra (scalar product excluded); out of spec.
